items.answer: Budi finished writing essays.

items.answer: Budi decided to apply for a scholarship.

items.sentence: She agreed to buy a new laptop.

items.sentence: They refused to cooking dinner for their family.

items.explain: After to, use the base verb: to cook, not to cooking.

items.answer: They refused to cook dinner for their family.

items.sentence: My parents dislike cook dinner for their family.

items.answer: My parents dislike cooking dinner for their family.

items.explain: Dislike is followed by -ing: dislike writing.

items.explain: Enjoy is followed by -ing: enjoy reading.

items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider applying.

items.explain: Enjoy is followed by -ing: enjoy learning.

items.explain: Enjoy is followed by -ing: enjoy learning.

items.corrected: My friends avoided buying a new laptop.
items.explain: Avoid is followed by -ing: avoid buying.

items.answer: My friends avoided buying a new laptop.
items.explain: Avoid is followed by -ing: avoid buying.

items.corrected: She enjoys studying English every evening.
items.explain: Enjoy is followed by -ing: enjoy studying.

items.answer: She enjoys studying English every evening.
items.explain: Enjoy is followed by -ing: enjoy studying.

items.sentence: My parents agree to visiting their grandparents.
items.corrected: My parents agree to visit their grandparents.
items.explain: After to, use the base verb: to visit, not to visiting.

items.answer: My parents agree to visit their grandparents.
items.explain: Agree is followed by to + base verb: agree to visit.

items.sentence: Andi plans to visiting his grandparents.
items.corrected: Andi plans to visit his grandparents.
items.explain: After to, use the base verb: to visit, not to visiting.

items.answer: Andi plans to visit his grandparents.

items.corrected: Dewi planned to apply for a scholarship.
items.explain: After to, use the base verb: to apply, not to applying.

items.answer: Dewi planned to apply for a scholarship.
items.explain: Plan is followed by to + base verb: plan to apply.

items.sentence: She learns to writing essays.
items.corrected: She learns to write essays.
items.explain: After to, use the base verb: to write, not to writing.

items.answer: She learns to write essays.
items.explain: Learn is followed by to + base verb: learn to write.

items.sentence: My parents promise to write essays.
items.corrected: My parents promise to write essays.
items.explain: Correct. Promise is followed by to + base verb: promise to write.

items.answer: My parents promise to write essays.
items.explain: Promise is followed by to + base verb: promise to write.

items.sentence: I considered apply for a scholarship.
items.corrected: I considered applying for a scholarship.
items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider applying.

items.answer: I considered applying for a scholarship.
items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider applying.

items.corrected: My parents consider applying for a scholarship.
items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider applying.

items.answer: My parents consider applying for a scholarship.
items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider applying.

items.sentence: He practiced write essays.
items.corrected: He practiced writing essays.
items.explain: Practice is followed by -ing: practice writing.

items.answer: He practiced writing essays.
items.explain: Practice is followed by -ing: practice writing.

items.answer: Andi considered taking the IELTS test.
items.explain: Consider is followed by -ing: consider taking.

items.answer: She disliked cooking dinner for her family.
items.explain: Dislike is followed by -ing: dislike cooking.

items.answer: We hoped to buy a new laptop.
items.explain: Hope is followed by to + base verb: hope to buy.

items.sentence: My father ___ coffee every morning.
items.answer: drinks
items.explain: One person (he/she/it) takes verb + s in the present simple.

items.answer: She doesn't like spicy food.
alts: She does not like spicy food.
items.wrong: She don't like spicy food.
items.explain: With he, she or it, the negative is doesn't (does not).

items.answer: We usually eat dinner at seven.
items.explain: Frequency words (usually, always, never) go before the main verb.

items.sentence: Everybody ___ happy today.
items.answer: is
items.explain: Everybody and everyone take a singular verb.

items.answer: The price of these shoes is too high.
items.wrong: The price of these shoes are too high.
items.explain: The subject is the price (one thing), not the shoes, so use is.

items.answer: She never drinks coffee at night.
items.explain: Never goes before the main verb, and the verb still takes -s.

items.sentence: Look! The children ___ in the rain.
items.answer: are playing
items.explain: For something happening now, use am/is/are + verb-ing. Children is plural, so are.

items.sentence: I am study English right now.
items.corrected: I am studying English right now.
items.explain: After am/is/are for an action happening now, use the -ing form.

items.sentence: She didn't come to class yesterday.
items.corrected: She didn't come to class yesterday.
items.explain: Correct: didn't + base verb (come).

items.answer: Did you see the movie?
items.wrong: Did you saw the movie?
items.explain: After did, use the base verb. Did already shows the past.

items.answer: I didn't go to school yesterday.
alts: I did not go to school yesterday.
items.wrong: I didn't went to school yesterday.
items.explain: After didn't, use the base verb: didn't go.

items.sentence: Can you close ___ door, please?
items.answer: the
items.explain: Use the when both people know which one you mean.

items.answer: Can you open the window, please?
alts: Can you open the window please?
items.wrong: Can you open window, please?
items.explain: A single countable noun needs a, an or the. Both people know which window, so use the.

items.sentence: The sun is ___ star.
items.answer: a
items.explain: Use a/an to say what kind of thing something is.

items.sentence: She gave me many informations.
items.corrected: She gave me a lot of information.
items.explain: Information is uncountable: no -s and no a/an. Say a lot of information.

items.answer: I need some advice.
items.wrong: I need some advices.
items.explain: Advice is uncountable: no -s.

items.sentence: There isn't much ___ in the fridge.
items.answer: milk
items.explain: Milk is uncountable: no -s and no a/an.

items.answer: I agree with you.
items.wrong: I am agree with you.
items.explain: Agree is already a verb. Don't put am/is/are before a normal verb.

items.answer: My sister is very smart.
items.wrong: My sister very smart.
items.explain: Before an adjective, English needs am/is/are.

items.sentence: My mother is a teacher. ___ works at a high school.
items.answer: She
items.explain: He is for a man or boy, she is for a woman or girl.

items.answer: My aunt said she is busy.
alts: My aunt said she was busy.
items.wrong: My aunt said he is busy.
items.explain: An aunt is a woman, so use she.

items.sentence: I was born ___ 2001.
items.answer: in
items.explain: Years and months take in: in 2001, in May.

items.sentence: The shop closes ___ 9 p.m.
items.answer: at
items.explain: Clock times take at.

items.sentence: We have a party ___ my birthday.
items.answer: on
items.explain: Specific days and dates take on: on my birthday, on Monday.

items.answer: Where do you live?
items.explain: Question pattern: question word + do/does + subject + verb.

items.answer: Why are you late?
items.wrong: Why you are late?
items.explain: In questions, am/is/are goes before the subject.

items.sentence: What time does the bus leave?
items.corrected: What time does the bus leave?
items.explain: Correct: does + subject + base verb (leave).

items.sentence: Look at those clouds. It ___ rain.
items.answer: is going to
items.explain: Use going to when you can see now that something will happen.

items.answer: I will call you tomorrow.
alts: I'll call you tomorrow.
items.wrong: I will to call you tomorrow.
items.explain: After will, use the base verb with no to.

items.sentence: She is taller that her brother.
items.corrected: She is taller than her brother.
items.explain: Comparisons use than: taller than, cheaper than.

items.answer: There are twenty students in my class.
alts: In my class, there are twenty students.
items.wrong: In my class have twenty students.
items.explain: To say something exists, use there is / there are, not have.

items.sentence: He speaks very good.
items.corrected: He speaks very well.
items.explain: Good is an adjective. To describe how someone speaks, use the adverb well.

items.sentence: The team ___ analyzed the research data.
items.answer: carefully
items.explain: An adverb describes the verb (analyzed): carefully.

items.sentence: The number of students increased ___.
items.answer: significantly
items.explain: Use an adverb after a verb to describe how something changed: increased significantly.

items.sentence: I live in a ___ city near the capital.
items.answer: small
items.explain: Use an adjective before a noun: a small city.

items.answer: He works very hard.
items.wrong: He works very hardly.
items.explain: Hard is already an adverb: work hard. Hardly means almost not.

items.sentence: He didn't study, ___ he passed the exam.
items.answer: yet
items.explain: Yet shows an unexpected contrast.

items.sentence: She was angry, ___ she was very hungry.
items.answer: for
items.explain: For (formal) gives a reason, like because.

items.sentence: Would you like tea, ___ do you prefer coffee?
items.answer: or
items.explain: Or offers a choice.

items.sentence: He doesn't eat meat, ___ does he drink milk.
items.answer: nor
items.explain: Nor adds a second negative idea. After nor, the word order is like a question: nor does he.

items.answer: I like playing football, but I don't like basketball.
alts: I like to play football, but I don't like basketball.
items.wrong: I like play football, I don't like basketball.
items.explain: Join two contrasting clauses with but. Also: like playing (or like to play).

items.answer: The library was closed, so we studied at home.
items.explain: Compound sentence: clause + comma + so + clause.

items.answer: I read books because they help me relax.
items.explain: Complex sentence: main clause + because + reason.

items.sentence: My sister and her friend ___ in Jakarta.
items.answer: live
items.explain: Two subjects joined by and are plural.

items.sentence: Everyone in the class ___ submitted their essay.
items.answer: has
items.explain: Everyone is singular, so use has.

items.sentence: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
items.answer: is
items.explain: Neither of … takes a singular verb in formal English.

items.sentence: All the students ___ waiting outside.
items.answer: are
items.explain: All the students is plural.

items.sentence: Nothing ___ impossible with practice.
items.answer: is
items.explain: Nothing is singular.

items.sentence: The number of tourists ___ increased every year.
items.answer: has
items.explain: The number of … is singular (one number). A number of … is plural.

items.sentence: A number of students ___ absent today.
items.answer: are
items.explain: A number of … means many, so it is plural.

items.sentence: The sun ___ in the east.
items.answer: rises
items.explain: General truths use the present simple.

items.sentence: More students ___ abroad these days.
items.answer: are studying
items.explain: These days shows a changing trend, so use the present continuous.

items.answer: I'm currently preparing for the IELTS exam.
items.explain: Currently = now, so use am/is/are + -ing.

items.sentence: I ___ when he called.
items.answer: was reading
items.explain: Longer action in progress: was/were + -ing. Short action: past simple (called).

items.sentence: When I was younger, I ___ football every weekend.
items.answer: played
items.explain: A repeated finished habit in the past uses the past simple.

items.sentence: While she ___ dinner, the lights went out.
items.answer: was cooking
items.explain: While + past continuous for the longer background action.

items.sentence: I ___ my friend tomorrow at 10. We booked a table.
items.answer: am meeting
items.explain: For an arranged plan with a time, use the present continuous: I'm meeting.

items.sentence: I think it ___ tomorrow.
items.answer: will rain
items.explain: For a prediction (I think…), use will.

items.sentence: I'm ___ apply for a scholarship next year. I have already decided.
items.answer: going to
items.explain: For a plan you already decided, use be going to.

items.answer: I am going to continue my studies after graduation, and I think it will be fun.
items.wrong: I am going to continue my studies after graduation, I think it is will be fun.
items.explain: Don't put is before will: it will be. Join the two clauses with and.

items.sentence: I have known her ___ 2010.
items.answer: since
items.explain: Since + a starting point (2010).

items.sentence: I saw him ___.
items.answer: last week
items.explain: Past simple goes with a finished time like last week.

items.answer: I have not eaten since yesterday.
alts: I haven't eaten since yesterday.
items.wrong: I have not ate since yesterday.
items.explain: After have, use the past participle: eat → ate → eaten.

items.answer: Barra has eaten a burger.
items.wrong: Barra have eaten a burger.
items.explain: One person takes has: Barra has eaten.

items.answer: The teacher who helped me with my essay is kind.
alts: The teacher, who is kind, helped me with my essay.
items.wrong: The teacher is kind, she helped me with my essay.
items.explain: Join the ideas with who instead of two sentences glued with a comma.

items.answer: The book which is on the table belongs to Sarah.
alts: The book that is on the table belongs to Sarah.
The book, which is on the table, belongs to Sarah.
The book on the table belongs to Sarah.
items.wrong: The book is on the table. It belongs to Sarah.
items.explain: Use which (or that) to join the two sentences.

items.answer: The book, which was written in 1990, has become a classic.
items.explain: Extra information about a thing: comma + which + clause + comma.

items.sentence: If I ___ harder, I would have passed.
items.answer: had studied
items.explain: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

items.answer: If I wake up late, I will miss the bus.
items.explain: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb.

items.answer: If I'm late for class, my teacher will be angry.
items.explain: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb.

items.sentence: The cake ___ in the oven at 180 degrees.
items.answer: is baked
items.explain: Describing a process: present passive (is + past participle).

items.sentence: A new product ___ by the company next year.
items.answer: will be launched
items.explain: Future passive: will be + past participle.

items.sentence: The dinner ___ by the chef right now.
items.answer: is being prepared
items.explain: Passive continuous: is being + past participle.

items.sentence: A new strategy ___ by experts.
items.answer: has been developed
items.explain: Passive perfect: has been + past participle.

items.sentence: The manager had the report ___ by the assistant.
items.answer: prepared
items.explain: Causative: have + object + past participle.

items.sentence: The results ___ tomorrow.
items.answer: will be announced
items.explain: Future passive: will be + past participle.

items.sentence: ___ sun rises in the east.
items.answer: The
items.explain: There is only one sun, so use the.

items.sentence: I am going to ___ university next year.
items.explain: Go to university / school / work / bed (to study, learn, work, sleep): no article.

items.sentence: She has ___ wisdom to succeed.
items.explain: Wisdom is uncountable and general here: no article.

items.sentence: ___ information is power.
items.explain: Information in general: uncountable, no article.

items.sentence: I saw ___ book on the table.
items.answer: a
items.explain: First mention of one book (any book): a.

items.sentence: Can you pass me ___ salt, please?
items.answer: the
items.explain: Both people know which salt (the one on the table): the.

items.sentence: Jakarta is ___ capital of Indonesia.
items.answer: the
items.explain: A country has only one capital: the capital.

items.sentence: She plays ___ piano very well.
items.answer: the
items.explain: Musical instruments take the: play the piano.

items.sentence: He plays ___ football every Sunday.
items.explain: Sports take no article: play football.

items.answer: I am going to university.
items.wrong: I am going to a university.
items.explain: Go to university (to study): no article.

items.sentence: There are ___ people in the meeting.
items.answer: many
items.explain: People is countable: many.

items.sentence: He has very ___ money, so he can't buy a car.
items.answer: little
items.explain: Money is uncountable: little (not few).

items.sentence: There is ___ work to do.
items.answer: much
items.explain: Work is uncountable: much.

items.sentence: She has ___ experience in teaching.
items.answer: a lot of
items.explain: Experience (skill) is uncountable: a lot of or much, not many.

items.answer: I need some advice about my essay.
items.wrong: I need some advices about my essay.
items.explain: Advice is uncountable: no -s.

items.answer: Although fast food is unhealthy, people like it.
alts: People like fast food. However, it is unhealthy.
People like fast food although it is unhealthy.
People like fast food, but it is unhealthy.
Even though fast food is unhealthy, people like it.
People like fast food even though it is unhealthy.
items.wrong: People like fast food. It is unhealthy.
items.explain: Show the contrast with although, even though, however or but.

items.sentence: I like coffee, ___ she prefers tea.
items.answer: whereas
items.explain: Whereas compares two different facts in one sentence.

items.sentence: The course was expensive. ___, it was worth it.
items.answer: However
items.explain: However shows contrast.

items.answer: She likes to dance, to sing, and to cook.
alts: She likes dancing, singing, and cooking.
She likes to dance, sing, and cook.
She likes dancing, singing and cooking.
She likes to dance, to sing and to cook.
items.wrong: She likes to dance, singing, and to cook.
items.explain: Items in a list need the same form.

items.answer: Online education is popular. It is also convenient.
alts: Online education is popular. It is convenient.
Online education is popular. This is convenient.
Online education is popular, and it is convenient.
items.wrong: Online education is popular. Online education is convenient.
items.explain: Use it (or this) to avoid repeating the noun.

items.answer: Pollution is increasing. It affects health.
alts: Pollution is increasing. This affects health.
Pollution is increasing, and it affects health.
items.wrong: Pollution is increasing. Pollution affects health.
items.explain: Use it (or this) to avoid repeating the noun.

items.answer: We discussed the problem.
alts: We talked about the problem.
items.wrong: We discussed about the problem.
items.explain: Discuss takes no preposition: discuss something. (Talk about something.)

items.answer: She is married to a doctor.
items.wrong: She is married with a doctor.
items.explain: Married to, not married with.

items.sentence: I'm good ___ playing the piano.
items.answer: at
items.explain: Good at + skill.

items.sentence: I will arrive ___ 10 a.m.
items.answer: at
items.explain: Clock times take at.

items.sentence: She lives ___ Paris.
items.answer: in
items.explain: Cities take in.

items.sentence: I am ___ the bus stop.
items.answer: at
items.explain: A specific point or location: at the bus stop.

items.sentence: Today is the ___ day of the week.
items.answer: hottest
items.explain: Hot → hotter → hottest: double the t.

items.sentence: This course is ___ than the other one.
items.answer: more interesting
items.explain: Long adjectives use more: more interesting.

items.sentence: I enjoy ___ books in my free time.
items.answer: reading
items.explain: Enjoy + -ing.

items.sentence: She plans ___ to Japan next year.
items.answer: to travel
items.explain: Plan + to + base verb.

items.answer: I like playing soccer.
alts: I like to play soccer.
items.wrong: I like to playing soccer.
items.explain: Like + -ing or like + to + base verb. Never to + -ing.

items.answer: He decided to study French.
items.wrong: He decided to studying French.
items.explain: Decide + to + base verb.
